subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Independent Training Cycle: Plan, Execute, Adjust
essentialQuestion: Can I run a full cycle without anyone checking on me?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of planning a cycle the learner will run unsupervised in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe self-monitoring by feel, performance, and adherence using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply pre-committed rules for progressing, holding, and deloading in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving diagnosing a stalled cycle; correct it and explain why.
Connect adjusting mid-cycle without abandoning the plan with honest evaluation, including of a cycle that did not work and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Run a complete self-directed training cycle end to end, documenting every adjustment and its reason, and write an honest evaluation of what worked and what did not.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Goal, modality, and volume are the learner’s; any medical restriction is planned around with guardian input.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
